campaign.dscr: Western Europe in 1070: England and Normandy, Capetian France, the Holy Roman Empire, Iberian taifas and Sancho II's Castile. Leon and Galicia remain separate. Approximate geographic provinces; grey lands are separate independent polities.

factions.dscr: Separate independent polities; shared grey is a game convention, not one state.
William I rules England and Normandy after 1066. Wales and Scotland remain independent.
Philip I's realm groups the great southern fiefs under nominal Capetian sovereignty, without implying direct royal administration.
Henry IV is King of the Romans, not yet emperor. Duchies and imperial Italy are grouped under one playable faction.
Separate Iberian taifas share a playable colour. Al-Mutamid rules Seville, not a united al-Andalus; the Almoravid intervention lies in the future.
Sancho II rules Castile in 1070. Leon and Galicia are separate crowns; Portucale is not an independent Portuguese kingdom.

campaign.dscr: Britain and the northern seas in 1050: Edward the Confessor, William of Normandy, Harald Hardrada and Macbeth. Denmark is independent of Norway. Approximate geographic provinces; grey lands are separate independent polities.

factions.dscr: Separate independent polities; shared grey is a game convention, not one state.
Edward rules England before 1066. Wales and the Scottish kingdom remain outside English ownership; northern earldoms are grouped under the crown.
William rules Normandy before his conquest of England. The two provinces divide the duchy for strategy play.
Harald rules Norway. Sweyn II's Denmark is separate and is not a Norwegian starting possession.
Macbeth rules Alba in 1050. Galloway and Cumbria remain separate frontier polities in this coarse reconstruction.

campaign.dscr: Ireland in 965: Dalcassian Munster, Leinster, Connacht, Ulaid and the Norse towns compete. Brian Boru is not yet king; the Norse towns share a playable grouping. Approximate geographic provinces; grey lands are separate independent polities.

factions.dscr: Separate independent polities; shared grey is a game convention, not one state.
Mathgamain, Brian Boru's elder brother, leads the Dalcassians in 965. Southern Munster remains separately governed.
Leinster is divided among dynastic branches. These provinces are a coarse playable grouping.
Connacht is represented as a provincial kingdom under Fergal mac Airt Ua Ruairc, before the later Ua Conchobair succession.
Ulaid is the eastern kingdom, not all modern Ulster. Northern Ui Neill lands in Tyrone and Donegal remain separate.
Amlaib Cuaran rules Dublin. Limerick, Waterford and Wexford are separate Norse centres grouped for play, not a single unified kingdom.

campaign.dscr: Iberia in 1180: Leon, Castile, Aragon and Portugal face the Almohad caliphate. The Balearic Banu Ghaniya and Navarre remain separate. Approximate geographic provinces; grey lands are separate independent polities.

factions.dscr: Separate independent polities; shared grey is a game convention, not one state.
Leon and Galicia form Ferdinand II's realm; Castile remains a separate crown.
Alfonso VIII holds Toledo and Cuenca, captured in 1177. Southern Iberia remains Almohad.
Aragon and the county of Barcelona are united under Alfonso II. Navarre is separate.
Portugal holds Lisbon and the Evora frontier. The Algarve remains outside its starting realm; the frontier is coarse.
The Almohads hold much of al-Andalus and the Maghrib. The Balearic Banu Ghaniya remain independent.

campaign.dscr: Italy in 1050: Henry III's imperial sphere, Norman newcomers, Pope Leo IX, divided Sicily and Byzantine southern Italy. Papal and Norman possessions are represented before their later expansion. Approximate geographic provinces; grey lands are separate independent polities.

factions.dscr: Separate independent polities; shared grey is a game convention, not one state.
The imperial sphere groups northern Italy and its marches. Local bishops, margraves and cities retain substantial autonomy; Venice remains separate.
Drogo leads the Norman county centred on Melfi. Capua and Benevento have not yet become Norman principalities; the Norman Marches aggregate scattered holdings.
Pope Leo IX holds the Roman core. Benevento and the later papal Romagna are not assigned as consolidated papal territory in 1050.
Sicily is divided among Muslim rulers. A shared faction is an abstraction under the name of the late Kalbid emir, not a unified central administration.
Constantine IX is the imperial ruler; local catepans command in Italy. Byzantine Calabria and the remaining catepanate face Norman encroachment. The Norman-controlled inland marches are separate.

campaign.dscr: The eastern Mediterranean in 1070, before Manzikert: Byzantium retains its Balkan and Anatolian provinces, the Great Seljuqs advance in the east, and the Fatimids hold Egypt and Palestine. Approximate geographic provinces; grey lands are separate independent polities.

factions.dscr: Separate independent polities; shared grey is a game convention, not one state.
Before Manzikert in 1071, the empire retains most Anatolia, the Balkan imperial provinces and its eastern cities. Frontier control remains contested.
Alp Arslan's sphere includes Iran, eastern frontier lands and Seljuq suzerainty in Iraq. Local dynasties and Abbasid Baghdad are grouped for campaign play.
The Fatimid core is Egypt and Palestine with a contested Syrian frontier. Arabian lands are independent; Damascus is not assigned to the later Seljuq conquest.
